title: NSW Office of the Children's Guardian releases Child Safe checklist for parents and carers
body: The NSW Office of the Children's Guardian has released a new Child Safe checklist designed to help parents and carers assess whether organisations are meeting child safe standards. The checklist provides practical questions and indicators for families to consider when choosing activities and programs for their children. Sporting clubs may find this resource useful for understanding what parents are looking for in child safe organisations.
source: NSW Office of the Children's Guardian

title: Huge surge in daycare centre visits amid safety crackdown
body: Australian regulators have significantly increased compliance visits to childcare centres as part of an ongoing safety crackdown, with hundreds of additional inspections conducted. While this development primarily affects early childhood services, it signals increased regulatory scrutiny across all child-focused sectors. Sporting clubs should expect similar attention to child safety compliance and record-keeping standards.
source: Australian Children's Education and Care Quality Authority

title: National Working With Children Check Reforms Agreed
body: All Australian states and territories have agreed to implement reforms to Working with Children Check systems by the end of 2025. The changes aim to close loopholes and improve information sharing between jurisdictions. Sports clubs should monitor their state regulator for specific implementation details.

title: NSW Removes Appeal Rights for Denied Working With Children Checks
body: NSW has introduced legislation removing the right to appeal denied Working with Children Check applications in certain circumstances. The change aims to strengthen child protection by preventing unsuitable people from accessing children through the appeals process. This affects how sports clubs may need to respond to workforce screening outcomes.

title: Victoria Passes Childcare Protection Legislation
body: Victoria has passed new childcare protection laws following safety reviews, though these primarily affect early childhood education settings. Sports clubs using childcare facilities or running programs for young children should review any overlap with their child safe obligations. The changes strengthen Working with Children Check requirements in childcare contexts.

title: National Continuous Checking System in Development
body: A national continuous checking system for Working with Children Checks is being developed to support reform across Australia. The system will enable real-time monitoring of cardholders against police and court records. Implementation timeframes and impact on sports clubs will be confirmed as the system is rolled out.

title: Queensland Blue Card System Legislative Changes
body: Queensland has introduced legislative changes to the Blue Card system affecting volunteer and paid workers. The changes impact application processes, continuous monitoring, and notification requirements for organisations including sporting clubs. Clubs should check with Blue Card Services for details on compliance obligations.

title: Victoria: Child Safety Reforms Strengthen Safeguards
body: New child safety laws took effect in Victoria in March 2026, strengthening safeguards for children in organisations including sporting clubs. The reforms build on Victoria's existing Child Safe Standards and introduce additional compliance requirements for organisations working with children.

title: Community Sport Volunteers Need Better Child Safety Support
body: New research published in March 2026 found that community sport volunteers require better support and resources to effectively keep children safe from abuse. The research highlights gaps in safeguarding training and implementation at grassroots sporting clubs across Australia.

title: Victoria: Updated Mandatory Reporting and Child Protection Obligations
body: Victoria has updated guidance on mandatory reporting and other child protection obligations for organisations working with children. The May 2026 update clarifies reporting requirements and organisational responsibilities under the Child Safe Standards.

title: Victoria: Child Safety Training Resources Updated
body: Victoria has published updated child safety training and resources to help organisations meet their obligations under the Child Safe Standards. The resources are available to sporting clubs and other organisations working with children.

title: Basketball Australia Launches New Child Safety Resources
body: Basketball Australia released new child safety resources in August 2025 to strengthen its safe sport commitment. The resources provide guidance for clubs and associations on implementing child safeguarding practices.

title: QRL Partners with Sporting Code Services on Child Safeguarding
body: Queensland Rugby League announced in November 2025 it is partnering with Sporting Code Services to support child safeguarding practices across community rugby league. The partnership aims to strengthen child protection standards at grassroots clubs.

title: NSW Children's Guardian Leadership Changes Following Inquiry
body: The NSW Children's Guardian stepped down in February 2025 following serious allegations and was formally dismissed in September 2025 after an inquiry. Sporting clubs in NSW should be aware that the Office of the Children's Guardian continues to operate and oversee Working With Children Checks and child safe standards compliance during this transition period.

title: NSW Government Announces Fines for WWCC Non-Compliance
body: NSW authorities have issued fines to tutoring services and modelling agencies for failing to verify Working With Children Checks. This enforcement action demonstrates increased scrutiny across all organisations working with children, including sporting clubs. Clubs should ensure all volunteers and staff have current WWCCs and that verification processes are documented.
source: NSW Office of the Children's Guardian

title: Aboriginal Foster Care Provider Loses Accreditation in NSW
body: An Aboriginal community controlled organisation providing foster care in NSW has had its accreditation stripped following concerns about child wellbeing. While this relates to out-of-home care rather than sport, it highlights the serious consequences of failing to meet child safe standards and the importance of robust safeguarding practices in all organisations working with children.
source: NSW Office of the Children's Guardian

title: eSafety Commissioner and Sport Integrity Australia strengthen focus on online abuse in sport
body: The eSafety Commissioner and Sport Integrity Australia have announced a strengthened partnership to tackle online abuse targeting athletes, coaches and officials. The collaboration will focus on education, reporting mechanisms and support for sporting organisations dealing with cyberbullying and harassment. Sporting clubs are encouraged to familiarise themselves with eSafety's resources and reporting tools.

title: Junior sport facing increased cyberbullying challenges
body: Reports indicate a growing trend of cyberbullying incidents in junior sporting environments, with concerns about social media misuse and online harassment affecting young athletes and their families. Clubs are reminded to have clear social media policies and processes for responding to online abuse. The eSafety Commissioner provides specific guidance and complaint mechanisms for sport related online abuse.

title: Kerala cricket coach sentenced to 35 years for child abuse
body: A cricket coach in Kerala, India has been sentenced to 35 years imprisonment for the sexual abuse of a minor trainee. While this case occurred overseas, it serves as a reminder of the importance of robust screening, supervision and reporting mechanisms in Australian sporting clubs. All clubs should ensure their child safety policies and Working With Children Check processes are up to date.

title: Sydney tennis coach barred over child grooming allegations
body: A Sydney tennis coach has been barred from the sport following child grooming allegations. The case highlights the critical role of Sport Integrity Australia and state sporting bodies in investigating and responding to safeguarding concerns. Clubs should familiarise themselves with complaint reporting pathways and interim risk management measures.

title: Basketball Australia rolls out Social Protect platform to NBL and WNBL
body: Basketball Australia has partnered with Social Protect to monitor online abuse and safeguarding risks across the NBL and WNBL. The platform uses technology to detect harmful content and protect athletes from online threats. Community basketball clubs may wish to consider similar tools as part of their broader child safety and wellbeing strategies.

title: Northern Football Netball League partners with SportsBuddy
body: The Northern Football Netball League has announced a partnership with SportsBuddy to support club compliance and administration. While details of the partnership's child safety features are not yet clear, clubs should stay informed about available technology solutions that can assist with Working With Children Check tracking and child safe policy implementation.
